about.title: Placerville Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Placerville sits along a corridor of active trade, logistics, and small-business work, from warehouses near US-50 to service crews moving along Placerville Drive and Broadway Drive. When a job-related injury happens here, most workers assume workers' compensation is their only option — and often it is. But California law also allows a separate claim when someone other than your employer contributed to your injury, such as a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer. With El Dorado County's mix of highway-adjacent commerce and rural job sites, third-party exposure isn't unusual. We handle workplace injury claims directly, reviewing both the workers' comp side and any possible third-party angle, so you understand the full picture of what you may be entitled to pursue.

items.title: Understanding Your Two Possible Paths
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can open a separate injury claim. We can help sort out which paths may apply to your situation.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury. Knowing this protection exists can make it easier to come forward within the required reporting window.

items.title: Awareness of Reporting and Filing Deadlines
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally must be reported to your employer within 30 days, while a separate third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt on a jobsite near Broadway Drive — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your primary route against your employer regardless of fault. But if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate third-party claim. We can review the details and explain which options fit your case.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Placerville?
items.answer: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Waiting longer can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it helps to report as soon as possible after the injury happens.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, we can help you understand your rights and next steps.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work on US-50 or Rt 50?
items.answer: Injuries during work-related travel can sometimes involve both workers' compensation and a separate claim against another driver, especially given the crash activity reported along these Placerville corridors. We can look at the specifics and help determine what applies.
